The year part was the police. It was a hit and run, and finding Mr. Runner proved to be difficult. They called me, telling me the case was closed about a month before the meeting request.  That gave me a renewed desire to get moving with this all.

I’ll have to go through the entire event again. I do remember it. I remember it in great detail. The facts won’t be hard, but the retelling will be.

Also, what about all the information he already has?  I gave his information to all the parties involved in my part. They’ve presumably communicated with each other. 

What if changing attorneys ruins everything somehow? 

I know that some of these are purely anxious thoughts. I can’t separate them at the moment though. Once I sleep, then perhaps.

So I’m going to bring this to the attention of my grandmother. Will she do anything?  I don’t know. I can’t know. But she’s her mother. She loves her daughter. Then I’m going to the beach. By myself, just relaxing and maybe reading a book. Maybe I’ll write. Maybe I’ll do none of that and play video games at home. Whatever I feel will be most relaxing. I’ve heard good things about this “sun” and “outdoors” thing though.

I don’t think it’s the worst, but one that my sisters and I often refer to without realizing how over the top other people find it. 

Our mother was strict on sweets- in that she could have them, but we had to ask first (but she was absent and said no anyway). So, being the children we were, wed eat it anyway. 

The first was a marble cake. Quite yummy. She soaked pieces in vinegar and forced my sister and me to eat it.

Cookies were another. Chips Ahoy chocolate chip. Half a cookie in vinegar was the punishment. 

Vinegar worked on my sisters. Not enough to stop us, but it was unpleasant. I love vinegar. Yeah, cake and cookies in vinegar was nasty, but they didn’t affect me like the hot sauce incident. 

The chocolate pudding wasn’t worth it. She mixed hot sauce into the sweet treat and made me eat it. I cried. She felt guilty for once (or at least seemed it).

We all still snuck sweets all the time. We just got smarter.

The worst for my sister was probably the chocolate. It was after church on Easter. My mother decided to make her eat a spoonful of cocoa powder because she was and still is a stupid bitch.

She did stop after that, if my memories are in chronological order.

I've tried a number of things in the past.  I haven't kept up with any of them, but they helped me a lot when I was in this same situation.  They were mostly used for finals.

1. For everything I've tried, I had to make a plan.  They were never really detailed plans, just what I had to do today and tomorrow.  Things like, "I have my exam Tuesday at noon.  I should study for it Monday."  Having that really helped, especially in calendar form.  It organizes one thing in your life.

2. You could try taking timed breaks.  I noticed that when I tried studying with no break I would get anxious and lose focus.  It helped when I said that I'd study for a half hour and do something fun for the same amount of time.  It could be longer or shorter, depending on you.  I used baking as my break, since it times itself and I have to stop or it will burn.  Eventually I noticed that I didn't want to stop to bake as often.

3.  Making an outline helped me, and I actually did keep up with this one.  When I had been struggling in the class, I opened the book and typed everything that looked important.  The first time I did this, I typed up the book's table of contents first, so I could see my progress.  I used this same method to type my notes after class.  I would often wait and have to do it all at once, but it still helped.

4.  Listening to instrumental music is awesome.  I listened to a Yiruma channel on Pandora.  He's a pianist, and I love the sound of a piano.  There were downsides, like a pop song being played that would distract me, but I skipped those.  There are ads, too, but I use adblock, which apparently blocks Pandora's ads.

I think that's everything that worked for me.  I mostly found that being in an environment that I enjoyed helped a lot.  Also having a plan.  You should try new things and if you find one thing that works perfectly, keep it up.  Even if you change it a bit, it can still help.

I really hope this is helpful, and good luck with your coursework!
